newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean fishing exports up nine pct Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: Chilean fishing exports up nine pct Jan-May.

text.p: Chilean fishing exports rose nine percent in the first five months of the year to $866 million from $795 million in the same period last year, the government reported.

The increase was in spite of a 10 percent decline in fishmeal exports, to $245 million from $272 million in the first five months of 1996. By volume, fishmeal exports slipped to 433,000 tonnes from 458,000 tonnes in January-to-May 1996, said the Fishing Under-Secretariat.
Fishmeal accounted for 28 percent of Chilean fishing exports during the first five months of the year. Chile is the world's second largest producer of fishmeal, an important animal feed, after Peru.
Main fishmeal export destinations in the period were Japan, accounting for 20 percent of exports, Taiwan at 15 percent and Germany at 14 percent of the total, said the under-secretariat.

Overall fishing exports dropped by volume to 642,000 tonnes from 688,000 tonnes in the first five months of 1996. The higher value of exports was accounted for by stronger shipments of value-added products like fish oil, smoked fish and processed seaweed, it said.

Frozen fish exports rose to $368 million in the first five months of the year, up from $284 million in the same period last year, while exports by volume rose to 94,000 tonnes from 84,000 tonnes, said the under-secretariat.
Refrigerated fresh fish exports rose to $115 million from $109 million previously, or by volume to 27,000 tonnes from 25,000 tonnes, said the under-secretariat.
